title: Two-role connection consistency
summary: Explore the student/professional invitation and confirmation journey with independent role identities and durable cross-role evidence.
allowedActions: Reset the declared owned professional/student fixture pair and verify both target identities
Sign in as the professional and expose the documented invite code through the UI
Sign in as the student, submit the code through the documented UI, and observe pending state
Return to the professional UI, confirm the request, and verify active state in both role contexts
Check the final relationship row through independent authenticated API and read-only SQL evidence
excludedExternalEffects: Production or shared identities, real customer contact, or external notifications
Direct database approval, privileged seed shortcuts, or changing a role outside the declared pair
Provider-console changes, purchases, issue posting, schedule creation, or destructive cleanup of unrelated data
Claiming cross-role consistency from one UI session or from generated connector output alone

scenario.title: Professional and student see the same pending-to-active relationship
preconditions: The professional and student accounts are independent members of the owned fixture pair
The relationship starts absent and the invite code is exposed by the professional UI
Both role sessions, API reads, and the SQL read are independently identified
actions: Read the invite code in the professional surface
Submit it in the student surface and capture pending state
Confirm the request in the professional surface
Read active state in both surfaces and through API/SQL
expectedObservations: The invite code and pending row belong to the declared independent identities
Confirmation changes one relationship to active without creating duplicates
Both role surfaces and independent API/SQL reads agree on the final row
Authorization or fixture blocks remain blocked and cannot be counted as a finding
